prompt:
A weather balloon is released from the ground and rises vertically. As it ascends, its upward velocity increases non-linearly with time, as shown on a velocity-time graph.
(a) Explain why the standard constant-acceleration equations cannot be used to determine the height of the balloon at a given time. [1 mark]
(b) Describe how the following quantities can be determined directly from the velocity-time graph:
(i) the instantaneous acceleration at t = 10.0 s; [1 mark]
(ii) the height of the balloon above the ground at t = 20.0 s. [1 mark]
hints: What assumption is required by the suvat equations?
How do you find the instantaneous rate of change from a curved graph?
How do you find accumulated displacement from any velocity-time graph?
solution:
(a) The constant-acceleration equations (suvat) are derived on the assumption that acceleration is constant, but the curved velocity-time graph indicates that acceleration varies with time.
(b)(i) Draw a tangent to the curve at t = 10.0 s and determine its gradient (delta v / delta t).
(b)(ii) Determine the area under the curve between t = 0 and t = 20.0 s (for example by counting squares or using numerical strip approximations).
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: For part (a), explicitly state that suvat equations strictly require constant acceleration, which is not present here [1 mark].
Step 2: For part (b)(i), state that instantaneous acceleration is found by drawing a tangent at t = 10.0 s and computing its gradient [1 mark].
Step 3: For part (b)(ii), state that height equals the area under the velocity-time curve between t = 0 and t = 20.0 s [1 mark].
